*tringgggg…* The alarm goes off early, and that doesn't make anyone happy. But for you, it’s not a problem! You get out of bed every morning with a big smile on your face. And we need that dose of kindness! :) Get started as a delivery driver at Albert Heijn in Bleiswijk. You make people happy every day! You have your own work van, and you also earn € 18,83 per hour! NICE! Do you want to know how to apply? #baanrader Then read on!

What we offer
- A top salary of € 18,83 per hour
- ​Loyalty program, get great discounts and presents
- Earn € 200, bring a friend!
- Flexible working hours
- Travel allowance
- A job with career opportunities!

Who you are
As a delivery driver for Albert Heijn, you are physically able to lift heavy crates. You enjoy working at different locations throughout the country if necessary! What you also need to know:

- You are available 12 to 14 hours per week
- You are available for at least two months
- You are available on at least two Saturdays per month
- You are willing to work in Amsterdam
- You speak Dutch or English
- You have held a Category B driving license for at least 6 months
- You are physically capable of lifting crates weighing up to 20 kg

What will you do
As a delivery driver for Albert Heijn, you are the shopping carrier on wheels! Your working day starts by collecting the key and the route list at the collection desk. The first days, you will ride along with a buddy. You quickly grab some food from the refrigerator. Then it’s time to hit the road! You drive to the right addresses via your navigation. Once you get here, you scan the correct crates with groceries with a handheld scanner. You bring the groceries to the front door. You just need to complete the payment and then you're ready to go! At the end of the day, you return to the depot. Here, you clean your bus for the next day. Do you have questions about the route? Then you can contact planning & support! :)

Working days: Monday to Sunday.

 Aan de slag bij De Haagse 
The Hague University of Applied Sciences (THUAS) is looking for a Researcher / PhD Candidate in agent-based modelling (ABM) on the circular economy . 
This is a 0.8 fte Researcher position at THUAS, with simultaneous enrolment as a PhD candidate at the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management (TPM) of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). 
About the position 
The candidate will be appointed for a 4-year period to research how to better understand and accelerate the circular economy. The focus is on developing a multi-level ABM that links micro-level consumer and organisational decisions to macro-level transition dynamics. Using inverse generative methods, the candidate will uncover which individual behaviours drive observed system-level transitions and build interactive policy dashboards to explore scenarios such as repair incentives and right-to-repair regulations. Case studies focus on e-bikes and washing machines. 
The position is embedded in CIVIC-4CE, a five-year NWO-funded consortium of universities, businesses, municipalities, and NGOs, and is conducted within THUAS's Centre of Expertise Digital Operations and Finance and the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management (TPM ) at TU Delft. Wat vragen wij van jou? 
We are looking for a candidate with an MSc in Complex Systems Engineering and Management, Engineering and Policy Analysis, econometrics, industrial ecology, innovation management, mathematics, computer science, or an adjacent quantitative field. Affinity with simulation modelling or programming is required; ABM experience is a strong asset.
